courses.prerequisite_raw: Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.
courses.course_overview_raw: Explore effective communication, both in-person and remotely, with customers, colleagues and stakeholders from different cultures. You will enhance your understanding of different communication styles that will reduce misunderstandings in a multicultural context. Through team based and individual learning activities, you will reflect critically on your own cultural identities, biases, attitudes and cross-cultural experiences and discuss how these factors may impact your effectiveness in a cross-cultural work environment. Learning objectives will be demonstrated through individual and collaborative assignments that will challenge you to analyze, reflect and evaluate your own identities and apply this knowledge to real world scenarios. Prerequisite(s): Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.

courses.prerequisite_raw: Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.
courses.course_overview_raw: Examine the role of leadership in developing and nurturing an effective global team. You will build on your knowledge of the impact cultural dimensions have on communication styles, working relationships, team performance, and leadership styles. Through collaborative and individual learning activities, you will analyze, practice, and refine the soft skills and strategies needed to create and lead high-performing global teams. Learn to recognize potential cross-cultural challenges, and develop strategies to mitigate them to enhance your leadership capacities and enable you to better manage and motivate cross-cultural teams. Competencies may be demonstrated through a blend of individual and collaborative assignments, skill demonstrations, and application to real world or hypothetical scenarios. Prerequisite(s): Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.

courses.prerequisite_raw: Admission into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership.
courses.course_overview_raw: Evaluate global strategic concepts that will enable successful leadership in a complex and rapidly changing global environment. You will analyze company strengths and weaknesses, assess risks and opportunities, and develop strategies for international companies. Through collaborative and individual learning activities, you will apply behavioural models to implement strategic change and overcome resistance to organizational strategic change. The objective of this course is to enhance leadership of strategy and to provide tools to develop effective business strategies and global goals to become an effective leader of strategic change. Competencies may be demonstrated through a blend of individual and collaborative assignments, skill demonstrations, and major papers. Prerequisite(s): Admission into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership.

courses.prerequisite_raw: Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.
courses.course_overview_raw: Innovation drives ongoing improvements and has the potential to unleash a new idea that can serve as a competitive advantage for an organization. It is thus important for business professionals to be able to identify the need and context for innovation, the roles key stakeholders play, how resistance will be managed, the communication styles that will be required and finally, the stages or timescale of innovation. Examine and evaluate the fundamental concepts of innovation management. You will be presented with the practical tools for developing an innovative mindset, with an emphasis on building and fostering a culture of creativity and innovation. Learn the skills needed to drive innovative initiatives in the workplace and cultivate awareness of the impact of change to individuals and organizations. Competencies may be demonstrated through a blend of individual and collaborative assignments, skill demonstrations, and quizzes. Prerequisite(s): Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.

courses.prerequisite_raw: Admission into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Explore the key elements of effective negotiation and conflict management. You will gain a deeper understanding of tools and processes that can be used to negotiate in a range of situations with internal and external stakeholders in a multicultural business context. Through collaborative and individual learning activities, you will develop strategies to resolve conflict in business and determine strategies that will increase team satisfaction and strengthen relationships. Competencies may be demonstrated through a blend of individual and collaborative assignments, skill demonstration, and exams. Prerequisite(s): Admission into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program.

courses.prerequisite_raw: Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program plus completion of Term 1.
courses.course_overview_raw: Drawing on the knowledge gained in the previous courses, you will assume the role of a Professional in Global Leadership. You will concentrate on real-world Industry challenges by engaging either in action or secondary research that will provide a professional learning experience. You will apply your Global Leadership skill set to the solution of the Industry challenge by working closely with a Faculty advisor and/or an Industry stakeholder. You will create a graduate level major report and presentation and evaluation will be based on application and integration of Global Leadership key concepts to the solution. Prerequisite(s): Acceptance into the Graduate Certificate in Global Leadership program plus completion of Term 1.

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted during the following periods: Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intake may fill before the deadline. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: A recognized bachelor's degree in any field Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand will require a basic evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success For the seminars to have graduate-level conversations and learning outcomes overall, it is expected students have some applicable life and/or work experience that can help conceptualize the theoretical and applied learning in the program. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program does not meet the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is therefore not eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. ( CIPC : 52.0213) Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
